title: Finite Tor amplitude descends from a finite principal localization cover
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $K^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of $R$-modules (modules $K^n$ and $R$-linear maps $d^n:K^n\to K^{n+1}$ with $d^{n+1}d^n=0$) [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $a\le b$ be integers. Let $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in R$, with $r\ge0$, generate the unit ideal, and write $R_{f_i}=R[1/f_i]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Use the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], specialized to the site with one object, only its identity morphism, and only the maximal covering sieve, so that sheaves of rings and modules are rings and modules. Derived tensor with an arbitrary module, placed in degree zero, is the ordinary-module derived tensor product computed on K-flat models by [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model]. If, for every $i$, the localized complex $K^\bullet\otimes_R R_{f_i}$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ (meaning that $H^n((K^\bullet\otimes_R R_{f_i})\otimes_{R_{f_i}}^{\mathbf L}N)=0$ for every $R_{f_i}$-module $N$ and every $n\notin[a,b]$), then $K^\bullet$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$: $H^n(K^\bullet\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M)=0$ for every $R$-module $M$ and every $n\notin[a,b]$.

proof.text: Fix an $R$-module $M$ and $n\notin[a,b]$. Apply [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on the singleton site specified in the statement to choose a K-flat resolution $P^\bullet\to K^\bullet$. By [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model], $C^\bullet=P^\bullet\otimes_R M$ represents $K^\bullet\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M$; since $M$ is in degree zero there is one tensor summand per degree.

source.place: Tag 066N, proof of lemma-glue-tor-amplitude; explicit K-flat computation of the displayed localization identity

proof.text: For every $i$, put $B=R_{f_i}$. The ring map $R\to B$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], tensoring with $B$ preserves exact sequences. In particular, applying it to the cycle and boundary sequences shows $H^q(X^\bullet\otimes_R B)=H^q(X^\bullet)\otimes_R B$ for every complex $X^\bullet$ and degree $q$: the kernel of the localized differential is the localized cycle module, its image is the localized boundary module, and their quotient is the localized cohomology. Thus $P^\bullet\otimes_R B\to K^\bullet\otimes_R B$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 066N, proof of lemma-glue-tor-amplitude; explicit K-flat computation of the displayed localization identity

proof.text: By [lem-pc-kflat-extension-of-scalars], $P^\bullet\otimes_R B$ is K-flat over $B$. Apply [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model] over $B$ to compute $(K^\bullet\otimes_R B)\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}(M\otimes_R B)$ by $(P^\bullet\otimes_R B)\otimes_B(M\otimes_R B)$. This complex is canonically isomorphic to $C^\bullet\otimes_R B$: in every degree the map sends $(p\otimes s)\otimes(m\otimes t)$ to $(p\otimes m)\otimes st$, with inverse $(p\otimes m)\otimes u\mapsto(p\otimes u)\otimes(m\otimes1)$. The balancing relations make these inverse maps well-defined, and the differential acts only on $p$, so they commute with differentials. The assumed local Tor-amplitude bound therefore gives $H^n(C^\bullet\otimes_R B)=0$.

source.place: Tag 066N, proof of lemma-glue-tor-amplitude; explicit K-flat computation of the displayed localization identity

proof.text: Since the finite family $(f_i)$ generates the unit ideal, [lem-pc-homology-vanishing-localization-span] applied to $C^\bullet$ gives $H^n(C^\bullet)=0$. This is $H^n(K^\bullet\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M)=0$ by step 1. Varying $M$ and $n$ proves the required amplitude bound. The vanishing criterion also covers $r=0$; then the unit-ideal hypothesis forces $R$ to be the zero ring.
